To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method that predicts GTP-, ATP-, SIA-, REA-, hNO-, and fNO-binding sites in proteins with high specificity and sensitivity, and we have applied this method to some 801 unannotated experimental protein structures, identifying 8 GTP-, 61 ATP-, 35 SIA-, 132 REA-, 33 hNO-, and 10 fNO-binding sites.

the LBS detection algorithm described in this article is able to predict the binding sites for GTP in small RAS-type G-proteens, ATP in ser-thr protein kinases (STPKs), SIA, REA, hNO and fNO in functionally unannotate protein structures in the PDB.

the algorithm we described previously (ibid.) is capable of predicting the binding sites of the 6 biologically relevant ligands we studied here, and that the cutting plane and the tangent sphere methods we also described previously (ib., ibid.) are capable of further validating the predicted binding sites.

our algorithm is a useful tool for structure-based protein functional annotation, especially for the 4 ligands (SIA, REA, hNO, fNO) for which no other structure-based functional annotation method exists.

the specific LBS algorithm we described previously (Reyes, VM & Sheth, VN, 2011; 2015) is a reliable and robust structure-based protein function prediction method, and that the 6 biologically relevant ligands we have screened for here can be reliably predicted using this method.

our algorithm can be used to predict the BSs of GTP in small ras-type G-proteens, ATP in serine/threonine protein kinases, SIA in sialic acid-binding proteins, REA in retinoic acid-binding proteins and heme-bound nitric oxide (Hb-NO) in heme-binding proteins.
